Subject: RAG evaluation follow-up: recommended retriever + reranker next steps

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on the discovery: you want improved grounding for product documentation answers (short, authoritative snippets), lower hallucination risk for sensitive pricing/legal queries, and better freshness for KB content.

Key recommendations we discussed (high level):
- Retriever: dense + hybrid approach (semantic ANN on top of BM25 fallback) — helps with recall on phrasing variations while keeping precision for short answers.
- Vector DB: prioritize the one you already run (we can integrate with your Pinecone/Weaviate/Redis setup) — we’ll send config examples.
- Reranker: start with a lightweight bi-encoder candidate score + a cross-encoder re-ranker for top-K (K=50->10) in the pipeline; tradeoff is throughput vs. factuality.
- Model family: for initial eval, we recommend Redwood-7b-quant for retriever-augmented generation tests (cost-effective) and Redwood-70b for higher-precision regression tests if latency/budget allow.

Deliverables we will share this week:
1) Prompt set + canonical prompt templates (attached: prompt_set_v2.jsonl)
2) Baseline eval CSV with current runs and metrics (attached: acme_rag_eval_v1.csv)
3) Reranker options and perf/cost tradeoffs (attached: reranker_proposal.pdf)

As next steps:
- Rishi will propose the exact retrieval + reranker pipeline config for you to run on a representative subset (~5k queries).
- If that looks good, we’ll run a full eval (10-50k queries) with the two model profiles.
- Schedule: can your team provide a 5k sample by EOD Friday? If so we’ll have the config and a demo run next week.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Rishi’s config and a shared Drive folder with the artifacts.

Hi Alex / Sam — following up with more detail and the config template I mentioned. Summary answers up front, then a config sketch and evaluation metrics.

Primary grounding metrics to prioritize:
- Precision@1 / Precision@5 (for short authoritative answers)
- Grounding Rate: percent of responses with at least one token span attributable to a retrieved doc (we compute via token overlap + citation mapping)
- Hallucination rate: percent of responses flagged by our factuality classifier or failed to match any retrieved source (measured on human-labeled sample)
- MRR / R-Precision for retrieval quality

Reranker guidance:
- Pipeline: dense retriever -> candidate set (K=200) -> bi-encoder fast re-score to K=50 -> cross-encoder re-rank top-K (K=10) -> generative model with citation injection.
- Thresholding: use a soft score threshold on the cross-encoder similarity; we typically set it to maintain recall (i.e., only prune when score < 0.12 normalized). For conservative setups we avoid pruning and only use the cross-encoder to reorder.
- Cost tradeoff: adding cross-encoder on top-50 will increase token-compute by ~3-6x vs. pure bi-encoder pipelines, but gains in grounding/factuality are often >10-15% on customer datasets. We can provide a per-1k-requests cost delta for your exact model choices.

Config sketch (attached in the Drive):
- Retriever: dense encoder (SBERT variant) with BM25 fallbacks; index refresh window 24h; ANN index (HNSW) ef=200 for production, ef_search=100 at eval time to speed up runs.
- Reranker: bi-encoder (distilBERT-based) for fast recalls, cross-encoder (roberta-large-ish) for reranking top-K = 10. We’ll also test a lightweight re-ranker using a distilled cross-encoder to trade cost/quality.
- Evaluation plan: run both Redwood-7b-quant and Redwood-70b on the sample with identical prompts + citation templates; capture token latency and cost.

Requested action from ACME:
1) Share 5k query sample to the Drive link (we’ll drop a folder and a readme).
2) Confirm which vector DB (Pinecone vs RedisVector) you prefer us to test first.
3) If possible, provide a prioritized list of 200 golden queries for human labeling (for hallucination measurement).

I’ve uploaded a quick script and config examples to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-rag-eval — Marissa will share the folder access.

TL;DR: start with cross-encoder only as an ordering signal (no pruning) to understand gains; if hallucination persists, we’ll tighten thresholding and run the heavier re-rank step.

Cheers,
